## 1. What this app is, what it does, and what it is for

`com.yftech.btphone` is the **Bluetooth phone user interface** of the YF Tech (GAC) head-unit — the screen the driver actually touches to make and take calls. It is a modern Android app (targetSdk 30, AndroidX, Kotlin, RxJava 3, ButterKnife, MVP architecture) rather than a bare service, but it is still `persistent=true` and `sharedUserId=android.uid.system`, and it still runs a `MainService` from boot. It does **not** implement Bluetooth itself: it is a pure client of the `car_bluetooth` binder service exposed by `com.yftech.service.bluetooth`, through the `com.yftech.car.bluetooth.CarBluetoothManager` facade. Its three screens are `MainActivity` (Contacts / Dial / Search tabs), `CallActivity` (in-call UI, multi-party, left/center/right layout) and `SearchActivity`, plus a set of always-on-top overlay windows for incoming calls that must appear over the navigation or CarLife screen.

**Purpose / why it exists on the device:**

The head-unit must present phonebook, call-log, dialling and call control without ever owning the Bluetooth stack (that is the `service.bluetooth` APK's job, and it must work identically across SoC vendors). This APK is the **presentation layer**: it keeps a cached, pinyin-indexed copy of the phone's contacts and call log so the driver can search them instantly, renders the in-call screen, and raises a system-overlay incoming-call dialog (`PhoneDialog`, window type 2054) so an incoming call is never hidden behind another app. It also carries the `EcallDialog` (emergency call) and `ContactsDetailDialog` paths, and a `TBoxViewManager` for T-Box related phone display.

**How it works (runtime flow):**

1. `BluetoothApplication` (extends the bundled `lib/sample/SampleApplication`) initialises `SoundPoolManager` (keypad/DTMF tones), a custom `CToast` with size 36sp / height 88 / params type 2054, then starts `MainService` and prepares `TBoxViewManager`.
2. `initProxy()` wires the four proxy singletons that the rest of the app talks to: `WindowManager`, `CallbackManager`, `DataProvider` and `PhoneCallWindowManager`.
3. `MainService` (extends `lib/sample/SampleService`) registers a `ContentObserver` on `Settings.System` keys `car_control_show`, `air_control_show`, `seat_control_show`. When one of them becomes 1 (i.e. the car/air/seat control screen has taken over the display), the service **force-finishes `CallActivity` and hides the phone-call overlay**, so an incoming call can never cover the climate or seat screen.
4. `MainService` also registers `GlobalReceiver` for action `com.yftech.btphone.action.REQUEST_ACTION`.
5. `DataProvider` holds the working model: `mContactBeanList`, `mTopContactBeanList`, `mCallLogBeanList`, `mPhoneCalls`, `mLetters` (the A–Z side index). It seeds two demo calls (10086 "客服" and 100861) and then refreshes from `CarBluetoothManager.getInstance().getPhoneCalls()`.
6. The MVP layer (`presenter/MainPresenter`, `PhonePresenter`, `SearchPresenter` + `contract/IMainView`, `ICallView`, `ISearchView`) drives `view/ContactsFragment` (pinyin `SideIndexBar` + favourites), `view/DialFrameLayout` with `KeyboardNumView` / `KeyboardView` (DTMF dialpad), and `app/CallActivity` for the active call with left/center/right call slots (multi-party conference) and a 1-second delayed finish.
7. `PhoneCallWindowManager` decides whether an incoming call should be shown full-screen or as an overlay dialog; `checkFirstIncomingCall()` suppresses the full-screen path when CarLife is in the foreground. `WindowManager` / `TBoxViewManager` own the actual overlay lifecycles.
8. `utils/SoundPoolManager` plays DTMF and ring tones, `utils/DialogManager` owns the modal dialogs (`CommonDialog`, `PhoneDialog`, `ContactsDetailDialog`, `EcallDialog`).

**Notable findings:**

- Depends entirely on the **`com.yftech.car.bluetooth` framework**, which is **not inside this APK** — `CarBluetoothManager`, `model.PhoneCall`, `model.Contacts`, `model.CallLog`. The Bluetooth work is done by `com.yftech.service.bluetooth` (see the `GAC_com.yftech.service.bluetooth.apk` repo).
- Uses a **system-overlay window (type 2054)** for the incoming-call dialog and the custom toast — the app can draw over everything, including navigation and CarLife.
- Deliberately **yields to vehicle control screens**: watching `car_control_show` / `air_control_show` / `seat_control_show` in `Settings.System` and killing the call UI when they are raised is a safety feature.
- Permissions include the non-standard **`beantechs.permission.DATATRACK`** (BeanTech = the CarLife/phone-link vendor) plus `com.yftech.permission.service.bluetooth` and `com.yftech.permission.service.transfer.phonelink` — this app is tightly coupled to the phone-link stack.
- Only 6 URLs are present and all are RxJava documentation links; the single IP is `127.0.0.1`; the only crypto primitive is `SHA256`. There is no analytics, no crash reporter and no tracking endpoint in the app's own code.
- `DataProvider.initPhoneCall()` seeds two hard-coded demo calls — "客服" on 10086 and "2222客服客服客服客服客服" on 100861 — a leftover developer fixture that ships in production builds.
- Tech stack worth noting for readers: RxJava 3 (`io.reactivex.rxjava3`), RxBinding 4 (`com.jakewharton.rxbinding4`), ButterKnife (`@BindView` / `@OnClick`, with generated `*_ViewBinding` classes), ConstraintLayout + MotionLayout, and a hand-rolled MVP framework under `com.yftech.btphone.lib` (base presenter/view/fragment, `sample/` reference implementations, `rx/` schedulers).
- 3075 Java files, but only ~22 packages / ~150 classes are YF Tech code; the remaining ~290 packages are AndroidX, Kotlin stdlib, RxJava and the support libraries.

## 3. Repository layout

```
.
├── README.md                  <- this file (full class/function catalogue + analysis)
├── sources/                   <- jadx: decompiled JAVA sources (.java)  **start here**
│   └── <package path>/<Class>.java
├── resources/                 <- jadx: decoded manifest + resources + assets
│   ├── AndroidManifest.xml
│   ├── res/                   <- layouts, drawables, values (near-original form)
│   └── assets/                <- raw asset files (config .properties, etc.)
├── smali/                     <- apktool: disassembled Dalvik bytecode (.smali)
│   └── <package path>/<Class>.smali
├── smali_classes2..N/         <- apktool: extra dex files (when present)
├── original/                  <- apktool: files that could not be decoded (META-INF, …)
├── AndroidManifest.apktool.xml<- apktool copy of the manifest (raw attribute order)
└── apktool.yml                <- apktool build metadata
```

`sources/` is the Java-readable tree — this is what you want to read. `smali/` is the same code in Dalvik assembly (useful when jadx output is ambiguous).
